ἐκβάλλω.definition: throw ashore, .. Od.19.278; .. .. Hdt.6.44; Id.7.170 :—Med., put ashore, Hdt.6.101; jettison, Syngr. ap. D.35.11

ἐκβάω.definition: Dor. for Foed. Dor. ap. Th.5.77

ἐκβλέπω.definition: look, Philostr.Jun.Im.I, cf; get the power of sight, Ael.NA3.25

ἐκβολβίζω.definition: peel, as one does an onion of its outer; metaph., uproot, destroy, Com.Adesp.992

ἐκβόλιον.definition: drug or other means for expelling the

ἔκβολος.definition: thrown out or away, exposed; frustrated, LXXJu.11.11

ἐκβυρσόω.definition: cause to project from the skin, Gal.18.721

ἐκβύρσωμα.definition: projecting of the bones out of the skin, ib.714

ἐκγελάω.definition: Ep. aor. h.Merc.389, Theoc.4.37; —laugh out, laugh loud, Od.16.354, 18.35, cf. X.Cyr.1.3.9, etc.; Pl.R.473c; Arist.Pr.965a24; metaph. of a liquid that rushes out with a gurgling sound, E.Tr.1176

ἐκγίγνομαι.definition: later and Ion. fut; c. dat., to be born to, .. Il.14.115, cf. Hdt.1.30,4.155; fut. perf., h.Ven.197

ἐκδέρω.definition: Ion. fut. strip off the skin; cudgel soundly, 'hide', Ar.V.450, Pl.R.616a, Hyp.Fr.200, PSI4.403 ; — Pass., Macho ap.Ath.13.580b

ἐκδέχομαι.definition: mostly of persons; take or receive from another, Il.13.710; A.Ch.762; of a beacon-fire, .. Id.Ag.285; take it on oneself, D.19.37

ἐκδέω.definition: bind so as to hang from, fasten to or on, c. gen., Od.10.96; they bound the oaks to the mules, i.e. they yoked the mules to them, Il.23.121; Aen.Tact.11.6; abs., bind planks behind, Od.22.174; E.Andr.556; metaph., tra…

ἐκδημέω.definition: to be abroad, to be on one's travels; c. acc., travel through, IG14.905

ἐκδημία.definition: going or being abroad, E.Fr.768: pl; metaph., departure from life, AP3.5

ἐκδίδωμι.definition: give out of one's house; give one's daughter in marriage, Hdt.1.196, E.IA132 , cf. Thphr.Char.22.4; having provided for their marriage at their own expense, D.27.69; D.S.4.53; freq. also without any acc., give in marr…

ἐκδιψάω.definition: to be parched with drought, of plants, Thphr.CP5.9.3; of a person, to be very thirsty, Plu.Cleom.29

ἔκδοτος.definition: given up, delivered, esp. betrayed; given in marriage, PMasp.5.10

ἐκδρομή.definition: running out, sally, charge, X.HG3.2.4; abstr. for concrete, party of skirmishers, Th.4.127

ἐκδύω.definition: causal in pres. impf. fut. aor. 1 late pf. AP5.72 :— take off, strip off, c. dupl. acc. pers. et rei, they stripped me of my cloak, Od.14.341; .. A.Ag.1269; X.Cyr.1.3.17; c. acc. only, strip, D.24.204; Id.54.8

ἔκζεσις.definition: boiling out or over, breaking out; = foreg., Erot. s.v

ἐκθάλλω.definition: put forth blossoms, Sm.Ca.2.13, Al.Hb.3.17; metaph., become active, of heat in the ground, Adam. ap. Aët.3.163

ἐκθεόω.definition: = , Ael.NA10.23, Porph.Marc.17; of temples or places, consecrate, App.BC3.3

ἐκθερίζω.definition: reap or mow completely, of a crop; cut out, Anacreont.9.7

ἔκθεσις.definition: exposure, of a child, Hdt.1.116; setting forth, exposition, Arist.APr.48a25, 49b6

ἔκθετος.definition: sent out of the house, sent away; projecting, salient, Sor.1.68; opp. Heliod.ap. Orib.49.4.23

ἐκθλίβω.definition: squeeze out, Arist.HA578b4, 626a20; Pass., to be crowded, cramped, of troops, X.An.3.4.19

ἐκθρῴσκω.definition: fut. aor. out of,c.gen., Il.16.427; 7.182, cf. 23.353; A.Pers.457; of the violent beating of the heart, 11.10.95; abs., leap forth, 21.539, cf. Corn.ND19; rarely c.acc., AP9.371; start up, Luc.DMar.2.3; come from the …

ἔκθυσις.definition: atonement, expiatory; averting by sacrifices, Iamb.Myst.9.3, cf.1.13

ἐκθώπτω.definition: aor. gain by flattery, wheedle over, S.Fr.857

ἐκκαθαίρω.definition: with acc. of the thing cleansed, clear out, Il.2.153; Hdt.l.c.; Hp.Mul.1.88, Orib.Syn.5.25.3; he clears this land of monsters, A.Supp.264; Luc.DDeor.13.1; clear him of all roughness, polish him up, metaph. from the fi…

ἐκκαλέω.definition: call out or forth, summon forth, Il.24.582; call forth, elicit, A.Ag.270; Aeschin.2.3; D.4.42, cf. Pl.Euthd.288d; Antiph.217.23; entice, provoke to battle, Plb.1.19.2, cf. Ascl.Tact.7.1

ἐκκαυλίζω.definition: pull out the stalk: metaph., pull off the sprouts, i.e. the profits, Ar.Eq.825

ἐκκείρω.definition: shear completely, shorn; cut off, A.R.4.1033

ἐκκενόω.definition: poet. empty out, leave desolate; unsheath, LXXEz.5.2

ἐκκηρύσσω.definition: Att. proclaim by voice of; cashier, 'drum out' of the army, prob. in Arist.Ath.61.2

ἐκκλέπτω.definition: aor. 2 Pass. X.HG5.4.12; —steal and; to deceive him, S.Ph.55, cf. 968; .. disguise not the matter, speak not falsely, Id.Tr.437

ἐκκλησία.definition: assembly duly summoned, less; = Lat. Comitia, = Comitia Centuriata, Curiata, D.H.4.20

ἔκκλισις.definition: turning out of one's course; tendency, Arist.Pr.863b24

ἔκκλυσμα.definition: that which is washed away, Plu.2.1089b; that which is washed up, produce of the sea, of purple dye, Zos.Alch.p.164 B. one must wash out, Aët.16.89

ἐκκναίω.definition: wear out: metaph. of troublesome loquacity, Theoc.15.88

ἐκκοπή.definition: cutting out, Phld.Ir.p.33 W; mutilation, Vett.Val.110.10

ἔκκριτος.definition: picked out, select, a chosen; evacuated, Arist.Pr.861a36

ἐκκυβεύω.definition: play at dice: metaph; Pass., to be gambled out of, lose at play, Plu.Art.17

ἐκκυέω.definition: bring forth, put forth as leaves, AP7.385

ἐκκυλίνδω.definition: roll out, Ar.Pax134; mostly; extricate, Pi.Fr.7, cf. AP7.176 :—Pass., to be extricated from, A.Pr.87; X.Cyn.8.8, cf. Plu.Galb.27

ἐκκυμαίνω.definition: swerve, bulge from the straight line, of a; cause to burst from their sockets, Herod.6.68

ἐκκύπτω.definition: peep out of, Babr.50.13; trans., put forth, Ael.NA15.21

ἐκλανθάνω.definition: escape notice utterly:—Med., forget utterly; causal in pres. with aor. 1 Aeol. : Ep. redupl. aor. 2

ἐκλεπτύνω.definition: make very thin, f.l. for Gp.16.6.3; reduce to a fine state, Syn.Alch.p.58B

ἐκλεπυρόω.definition: strip off the bark: metaph., strip, Sophr.22

ἐκλινάω.definition: escape out of the net, Eust.574.30

ἐκλογέω.definition: select, CPHerm.p.80; mostly in Med., excuse oneself, App.BC5.77; plead in excuse, ib.13: c. acc. et inf., to state by way of excuse that.., ib.3.48; Them.Or.8.103d

ἐκλύω.definition: v. set free, from labours; unloose, unstring a bow, Hdt.2.173; E.Hipp.825; likely to let loose a foolish tongue, S.Aj.1225

ἐκμυελίζω.definition: suck the marrow out of, deprive of strength, LXXNu.24.8

ἐκμυζάω.definition: suck out, Il.4.218, cf. Luc.Tim.8, Ael.NA3.39, Gal.UP6.15, Q.S.4.398; exhaust air from a vessel, HeroSpir. I Praef.: metaph., extort, Lyd.Mag.3.67; —also in form Dsc.Eup.1.62, Phlp.in Mete.115.18; —Pass., Antyll. ap. …

ἐκμυθόω.definition: make into a or fable, Philostr.Im.1.3

ἐκναρκάω.definition: become quite torpid or sluggish, Plu.Cor.31

ἐκνέμω.definition: pasture, Ph.2.233; —more freq. in Med; go forth to feed: metaph. in Med., S.Aj.369

ἐκνήφω.definition: fut. LXXGe.9.24; —sleep off a drunken fit; trans., carry off, LXXSi.34.2

ἐκξέω.definition: wipe off, erase, App. Anth.7.56,71, Tz.ad Lyc.874

ἔκπαγλος.definition: Ep. and Ion. word, terrible, violent; of persons, of Achilles, Il.21.589; also of Achilles, 1.146, 18.170; of other heroes, 20.389, 21.452

ἐκπαιφάσσω.definition: rush madly to the fray, Il.5.803

ἐκπαίω.definition: throw or cast out of a thing; intr., dash out, escape, Anaxil.22.17 :—Med., Plu.Brut.51

ἐκπαλαίω.definition: transgress the laws of wrestling, Philostr.Im.1.6

ἐκπατάσσω.definition: strike, afflict, E.HF890 : metaph., AP9.309 :—Pass., stricken in mind, Od.18.327; Hsch

ἐκπατέω.definition: withdraw from society, D.L.1.112; pf. part. having finished his walk, Id.4.19

ἐκπαύω.definition: strengthd. for set quite at rest, put an end to, E.Ion144 :—Med., take one's rest, Th.5.75

ἐκπέμπω.definition: bring out by calling, call or fetch out, Id.Ant.19:—so in Med., Id.OT951:—Pass., go forth, depart, Id.OC1664

ἐκπεράω.definition: abs., of an arrow, pass through, pierce, .. Il.13.652, cf. 16.346, etc.; of persons, go forth, X.Cyn.6.18; to Athens, Eub.10.5

ἐκπέρθω.definition: fut. destroy utterly, sack, of cities; take as booty from, Il.1.125

ἐκπέσσω.definition: Att. cook thoroughly: hence; of animals, digest or concoct food thoroughly, Hp.VM22

ἐκπέτασμα.definition: that which is spread out or; planisphere, Ptol.Geog.7.7 tit

ἐκπήδημα.definition: leap out, a height too great for over-leap, A.Ag.1376

ἐκπίεσμα.definition: that which is squeezed out; false form for , Gal.19.432, 14.782

ἐκπίνω.definition: fut. Amips.22.2; drain a cup dry, S.Fr.483; Pherecr.143.9; Antiph.3, etc.; also S.Ant.532

ἐκπίπτω.definition: of seafaring men, to be cast ashore, Od.7.283; Hdt.3.138; Id.8.13; E.Hel.1211; ib.539; Pl.Lg.866d; of things, suffer shipwreck, X.An.7.5.13; of fish, to be cast up, Arist.HA601b32

ἐκπλέω.definition: fut. pf. IG2.793a7; Ion; metaph., go out of one's mind, lose one's senses, Id.3.155, Ael.Fr.240

ἐκπνοή.definition: breathing out, exhalation, opp; death, J.AJ19.8.3

ἔκπνοος.definition: contr. breathless; breathing out, exhaling, Hp.Epid.6.6.1; smelling of.., Posidipp. ap.Ath.13.596c

ἐκποτάομαι.definition: Ion. = fly out or forth, of snowflakes, Il.19.357; of a ghost, Sapph.68.4: metaph., Theoc.11.72, 2.19

ἐκπτύσσω.definition: unfold, spread out, pf. part. Pass. prob. for Erot. s.v

ἐκπτύω.definition: fut. AP5.196 :—spit out; spit in token of disgust, Ar.V.792

ἐκπυρόω.definition: burn to ashes, consume utterly, E.IA1070; set on fire, Arist.Mete.341a18

ἐκπυρσεύω.definition: kindle, inflame: metaph., in Pass; give signals by a beacon-light, J.BJ4.10.5

ἐκραβδίζω.definition: flog out, drive out with a rod, Ar.Lys.576

ἐκρέω.definition: pf. : aor. Pass. in; of feathers, fall off, Ar.Av.104; of hair,Arist.HA518a32

ἐκρήγνυμι.definition: fut. S.Aj.775:—break off, snap; c. acc. cogn., let break forth, break out with, Plu.Fab.12; Luc.Cal.23:—Pass., break out, of an ulcer, Hdt.3.133; burst, of an abscess, Hp.Aph.4.82; .. A.Pr.369; of a quarrel, broke out…

ἔκρηξις.definition: breaking out, discharge; bursting asunder, Arist.Mu.395a15

ἐκσείω.definition: shake out or off; drive out or forth, Plu.Ant.14; reject it, D.S.18.66

ἐκσεύομαι.definition: Pass., pf. plpf. with sense of impf. , but usu. aor. : aor. I out or burst forth from, Il.7.1; Od.9.373; sleep fled away from his eyelids, 12.366: abs., rush out, Il.8.58; .. Od.9.438; the point burst out, Il.5.293 ; …

ἐκσηκόω.definition: weigh in the balance, assay, in Pass., Gloss

ἐκστρέφω.definition: turn inside out, Ar.Pl.721: metaph., change or alter entirely, Id.Nu.88; ib.554:—Pass., with feet turned outwards, Arist.Phgn.813a14; to be distorted, Gal.7.27

ἐκσῴζω.definition: Ep. :—preserve from danger, keep safe, Hdt.9.107, S.Aj.1128, etc.; E.El.28; to bring him safe.., Id.HF1222; Pl.Grg.486b:—Med., save oneself, Hdt.2.107; also, save for oneself, .. A.Pers.360; S.Ant.713:—Pass., .. when …

ἐκτανύω.definition: = Theoc.25.270:—Hom. has; extend, Epigr.Gr.1078.4 .— For S.OC1562, v. word, used by Hp.Fract.43. usu., but Anacreont.35.5 .]

ἐκτείνω.definition: fut. A.Pr.325, etc.:—stretch out; stretch, spread out a net, A.Ch.991; extend the line of an army, E.Heracl.801, Arr.Tact.5.6; E.Supp.654; X.HG6.5.19:—Pass., to be unfolded, smoothed, S.Fr.902

ἐκτελέω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.9.493, Od.4.7: Ep; of Time, Hes.Op.565, Hdt.6.69, Pi.P.4.104:—Pass., Od.11.294

ἐκτέμνω.definition: Ep. and Ion. , fut; cut trees out of a wood, cut down, Il.12.149, S.Tr.1196; also of planks, etc., hew out, hew into shape, Il.3.62, cf. 4.486; to cut the stumps out of the ground, Lys.7.19

ἐκτενής.definition: strained: hence of persons, warmly; extended, Dam.Pr.64; capable of extension, Herm.in Phdr.p.121A

ἐκτίθημι.definition: set up, offer for a prize, S.Fr.378; Plb.15.9.4; fix or grant allowances, rates of pay, etc., PSI5.498 , PEdgar2.4 , etc

ἐκτίνω.definition: Med., exact full payment for a thing, avenge, E.HF547; take vengeance on, Id.Med.267

ἐκτλάω.definition: bear, sustain to the end, aor.inf. Ph.2.464

ἔκτμημα.definition: section, segment, of the zones, Arist.Mete.362b5

ἐκτομάς.definition: wicket-gate, Aen.Tact.24.5; a kind of spear , Id

ἐκτομή.definition: cutting out, excision, Plu.Alc.16; castration, Hdt.3.48,49, Pl.Smp.195c , etc

ἔκτομον.definition: black hellebore, Hp.Mul.1.78; stone forming interior angle, Rev.Phil.29.240 , 49.6

ἐκτοξεύω.definition: shoot out, shoot away; metaph., reject, banish, Ph.1.528:—Pass., ib.252

ἐκτόπισις.definition: removal from a place, deportation, Gloss

ἔκτοπος.definition: away from a place, c. gen; foreign, strange, by no strange hand, S.Tr.1132

ἔκτρημα.definition: hole made in trepanning, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.16

ἔκτριμμα.definition: sore caused by rubbing; rubber, towel, Philox.2.41

ἐκτρόπιον.definition: everted eyelid, a disease in which the lid is turned outward, opp. Cels.7.7, Antyll. ap. Aët.7.74, Dem.Ophth.ib.73

ἔκτροπος.definition: turning out of the way. Adv. Erot. s.v

ἐκτυπόω.definition: model or work in relief; metaph. in Med., etc., form an image of a thing in . ., Pl.Tht.206d, cf. Lg.775d

ἐκφαίνω.definition: fut. Ion. in Luc.Syr.D.32: aor; of persons, bring to light, reveal, . . 19.104; produce him, Hdt.3.36; . . S.Ant.307, cf. OT329: c. part., Hdt.3.71; . . E.Hipp.428:—Pass., showed himself, came forth to view, Il.19.46,…

ἐκφατνίζω.definition: throw out of the manger: generally, throw; Med., eat out of the manger, Nic.Dam.p.3 D

ἐκφέρω.definition: fut. Hdt.3.71: Ion. aor; carry out a corpse for burial, Il.24.786, cf. Hdt.7.117, Antipho6.21 , etc.; also, cause death, Plot.1.4.8

ἐκφεύγω.definition: of persons accused, to be acquitted, Ar.V.157; c. gen., escape out of, Od.23.236; Epigr.Gr.1041.9; of things, Il.5.18: with Prep., APl.4.182

ἔκφημι.definition: speak out or forth, utter loudly:—Ep. only in Med., Od.10.246, cf. 13.308; A.R.1.439: later aor. 1 EM687.30

ἐκφθίνω.definition: in Hom. only in 3 plpf. Pass., the wine had all been consumed out of the ships, Od.9.163; 12.329; they have utterly perished, A.Pers.679 , 927

ἐκφλύζω.definition: or spirt out: c. acc. cogn., give vent to a groan, A.R.1.275

ἐκφοιτάω.definition: Ion. go out constantly, be in the; of things, to be spread abroad, Plu.Lyc.3

ἐκφορά.definition: carrying out, esp. of a corpse to; blabbing, betrayal of secrets, D.L.1.98

ἐκφορέω.definition: = carry out, as a corpse for burial; generally, carry out, Hdt.1.197, 9.116, Is.6.42 :—Med., take out with one, E.Cyc.234, etc.:— Pass., move forth, . . Il.19.360

ἐκφύω.definition: generate: mostly of the male, beget; rarely of the female, bear, S.OC984

ἐκχέω.definition: pour away: hence, spill, a vessel, Ar.Fr.306; Men.l.c.:—Pass., to be drained, PRyl.154.18

ἐκχιλόω.definition: cover all over with grass : land that bears nothing but grass, Paus. Gr.Fr.323

ἐκχολόω.definition: turn into bile, Herod.Med. in; Pass., to be charged with bile, Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.15

ἐκχορεύω.definition: break out of the chorus: generally, break; Med., drive out of the chorus, E.Hel.381

ἐκχράω.definition: declare as an oracle, tell out; suffice, Hdt.8.70: impers., c. inf., how will it suffice him, how will he be content to . . ? Id.3.137

ἐκχυμόω.definition: extract juice from, Hp.Morb.2.47; in Pass., of the small veins, shed the blood and leave it extravasated under the skin, Id.Fract.11

ἔκχυσις.definition: outflow, Arist.Mete.354a26; pouring; effusion of pus, Erasistr. ap. Gal.8.318

ἐκχωνεύω.definition: melt down, coin anew, D.C.68.15 codd

ἐκχώννυμι.definition: raise a mound, Aq.Ez.17.17:—usu. in Pass; of a bay, to be filled up by the deposit of a river, v.l. ib.11

ἐκψύχω.definition: fut. lose consciousness, swoon; to be short of breath, gasp, Arist.Pr.886b14

ἐλαιόμελι.definition: sweet gum from the olive-tree, Dsc.1.31,etc

ἐλαιόω.definition: oil:—only Pass., to be oiled, Arist.HA605b20; bring to an oily consistency, in Alchemy, Zos.Alch.p.163B

ἐλαίωσις.definition: treatment with oil or reduction to an oily consistency, in Alchemy, Zos.Alch.p.215 B

ἐλασία.definition: = riding, X.Eq.Mag.4.4; striking from a die, Gloss

ἔλασμα.definition: metal beaten out, metal-plate; general name for probes and other surgical instruments, Gal.2.574; ibid.: esp. flat end of a probe, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.11.3

ἐλαστρέω.definition: Ep. and Ion. for . . they drove the teams, Il.18.543; Thgn.600; to drive about, of the Furies, E.IT971; in later Prose, D.H.1.23; row, Ion. part. Arr.Ind.32.9:—Pass., of ships, to be rowed, Hdt.2.158, 7.24; cf. · Hsch…

ἐλατήρ.definition: driver, esp. of horses; rower, Luc.Am.6, Nonn.D.39.306

ἐλαύνω.definition: Il.12.62, etc.: Ion. impf; with acc. omitted, intr., go in a chariot, drive, he whipped them on, Il.5.366, al., cf. S.El.734,739; he drove on over the waves, Il.13.27; travel the night through, Od.15.50; drive into th…

ἐλαφίς.definition: a bird, perh. heron or egret, Dionys.Av.2.11

ἐλάω.definition: Ion. poet. pres. for v. init

ἔλδομαι.definition: and poet. Verb, only pres. and impf., wish, long, c. inf., Il.13.638, Od.4.162, Pi.O.1.4: c. gen., long for, Od.5.210; eager to reach it, Il.23.122: c.acc., desire, Od.1.409, cf. Il.5.481: abs., Od.24.400:—Pass. only …

ἐλεαίρω.definition: Ep. impf. Il.24.23: aor. 1 A.R.4.1308, Sammelb.2134:—lengthd. form of take pity on, Il.6.407, Od.10.399, etc.—Ep. word, used by Ar.Eq.793 , Luc.Trag.305

ἐλεγχής.definition: worthy of reproof; of men, cowardly; reproachful, Nonn.D.40.35

ἐλέγχω.definition: test, bring to the proof, B.Fr.10.2; A.Ag.1351 ; Pl.Sph.242b : with subject. clause, . ., A.Ch.851, Ar.Eq.1232

ἐλεέω.definition: impf. Apollod.Com.4.1: aor. Ep; abs.,feel pity, Ar.Ach.706

ἐλελίζω.definition: Ep. redupl. of , rare in; Med. and Pass., move in coils or spires, of a serpent, Il.2.316; 11.39, cf. A.R.4.143; Ar.Fr.500

ἐλεφαίρομαι.definition: old Ep. Verb, perh. connected with; of the Nemean lion, he used to destroy them, Hes.Th.330

ἑλίκη.definition: the constellation of the Great Bear, from its revolving round the pole, Arat.37, A.R.3.1195

ἑλίκων.definition: thread spun from the distaff to the; a nine-stringed instrument, Aristid.Quint.3.3, Ptol.Harm.2.2

ἑλίσσω.definition: or (the latter more freq. in codd. of; generally, roll, roll life's stream along, Pi.I.8.15; of the chariot of Day, A.Pr.1092 ; . . E.Ph.3; roll the eddying dust, A.Pr.1085 ; of the Euripus, E.IT7, cf.1103 ; Id.HF868 …

ἑλκέω.definition: = drag about, tear asunder, in impf. . . Il.17.395: also in fut. and aor. ib.558; 22.336; he did violence to Leto, Od.11.580; Arat.638:—Pass., Il.22.62

ἑλκηθμός.definition: being carried off, violence suffered, Il.6.465

ἕλκημα.definition: that which is torn in pieces, prey, E.HF568

ἑλκητήρ.definition: one that drags, of a harrow, AP6.297

ἑλκοποιέω.definition: make wounds or sores: metaph., rip up old; make an incision in a tree, Gp.5.38

ἑλκυσμός.definition: attraction; esp. of idle fancy; dragging, in pl., Anon.Fig.p.156 S

ἐξαγωγή.definition: leading out of troops, X.Eq.Mag.4.9; drawing out of a ship from shallows, Hdt.4.179

ἐξᾴδω.definition: sing out, sing one's last song, of the swan; sing the of a chorus, Plot.6.9.8

ἐξαθρέω.definition: look at carefully, dub. in Thesp. ap. Chrysipp.Stoic.2.55

ἐξαιμάσσω.definition: Att. make quite bloody; metaph., open one's griefs afresh, D.H.6.81

ἐξαίνυμαι.definition: take out or away, took out , Od.15.206: in Il. always in phrase animam eripuit, 5.155, al.; Nic.Al.272

ἐξαίρεσις.definition: taking out the entrails of victims; removal, purgation, Porph.Abst.2.43

ἐξαιρέω.definition: fut. later D.H.7.56, etc.: aor. 2; Med., take out for oneself, from his quiver, Il.8.323; their large sails, X.HG1.1.13; discharge their cargoes, Hdt.4.196; X.An.5.1.16; Th.8.90: abs., Syngr. ap. D.35.13, etc.:—Pass.,…

ἐξαίρω.definition: Ep. Hom. , also in Ion; seemingly intr., rise from the ground, of a bird, D.S.2.50; start, Plb.2.23.4, cf. LXXNu.2.9

ἐξακέομαι.definition: heal completely, Hp.Vict.3.67: hence, make; c. acc., appease, Il.4.36, cf. Od.3.145; quench, D.C.60.9; make up for, X.Cyr.8.2.22; Iamb.Myst.1.11

ἐξακούω.definition: hear or catch a sound, esp. from a distance; understand in a certain sense, Id.7.89

ἐξαλαόω.definition: blind utterly, Od.11.103; make blind and useless, Opp.C.3.228

ἐξαλαπάζω.definition: sack, storm, Il.4.40, 1.129, etc.; also, empty a city of its inhabitants, clear it out, so as to plant new settlers in it, Od.4.176: generally, destroy utterly, Il.13.813, 20.30: metaph., Theoc.2.85.—Ep. word, used by…

ἐξάλλομαι.definition: fut. LXXMi.2.12: aor; start from its socket, be dislocated, of a limb, Hp.Art.46; of a broken bone, Plu.2.341b; of wheels, start from the axle, X.Cyr.7.1.32

ἐξάλμυρος.definition: having lost its saltness, of earth, Thunell Sitologen papyri 1viii 11

ἑξαμερής.definition: in six parts, of the hexameter, Orph.Fr.356

ἐξαναβαίνω.definition: get to the top of, Artem.2.28; Epigr.Gr.782

ἐξαναβρύω.definition: causal of foreg., cause happiness to spring forth from the earth, A.Eu.925

ἐξαναδύομαι.definition: aor. 2 Act. rise out of, emerge; escape from, c. gen., Plu.Sert.12: c. acc., Thgn.1124; Orac. ap. Paus.4.12.4

ἐξαναζέω.definition: boil up with: c. acc. cogn., metaph., . . will let such fury boil forth, A.Pr.372

ἐξαναφέρω.definition: bear up, of buoyant sea-water; exhibit the form of a spear, Plu.2.563a

ἐξανεμόω.definition: blow out with wind, inflate:—Pass., to be; Pass., of corn, to be parched by wind, 'wind- bitten', Thphr.HP8.10.3

ἐξανθίζω.definition: deck as with flowers, paint in various; Med., gather flowers, Plu.2.661f

ἐξανίημι.definition: poet. impf. A.R.4.622: fut; c. gen., send forth from, Pi.P.4.99; E.Ba.762; Id.HF625

ἐξανύω.definition: conquer, App.Ill.15; of Time and Distance, bring to an end, finish, accomplish, S.Tr.1022 ; E.Med.649 ; Id.Ph.163 , Tr.232 , IT897 : abs. . finish one's way to a place, arrive at it, or . ., Hdt.6.139,7.183: also c. a…

ἐξαπαφίσκω.definition: Ep., = Hes.Th.537: aor. Od.14.379; subj. 23.79; part. h.Ap.379, h.Ven.38, E.Ion704 , Alex.Aet.3.19, etc.: Hom. also has 3sg. aor. opt. Med. in act. sense, Il.9.376, 14.160: later aor. 1 h.Ap.376, Q.S.1.137, Opp.H.3.94

ἐξάπλωσις.definition: opening out, of roots, Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.12; explanation, Erot.Prooem

ἐξαποβαίνω.definition: step out of, Od.12.306; A.R.3.199, etc

ἐξαπόλλυμι.definition: Pass., with pf. 2 aor. 2 utterly out of, c. gen., Il.6.60; 18.290; Od.20.357; A.Ag.528: abs., perish utterly, Hdt.4.173, S.Fr.236

ἐξαπολογία.definition: title of three speeches of Antipho, second defence, rejoinder

ἐξάπτω.definition: fasten from or to; metaph., let prayers fall from one's mouth, E.Or.383; consider actions as dependent upon chance, Plu.Sull.6; continue the narrative, D.L.8.50; dependent on it, Ti.Locr.102e

ἐξαράσσω.definition: c. acc. pers., assail him furiously with abuse, Ar.Nu.1373

ἐξαρθρέω.definition: dislocate the joints of; intr., to be dislocated, Hp.Art.29; suffer from dislocations, ib.8, 53

ἐξαρπάζω.definition: fut. Ar.Eq.708: aor.1 Hom; tear out, . . Ar.Eq.708; tear off, Asclep. ap. Gal.12.418

ἐξάρτημα.definition: that which is suspended from; that which is attached or dependent, Dam.Pr.130

ἐξάρτησις.definition: attachment of parts of the body one; suspension of a weight, Sor.1.72

ἐξάρχω.definition: begin, take the lead in, initiate, c. gen; hold office, Polem.Cyn.18; rule, c. gen., Eustr.in EN2.32

ἐξάρχων.definition: ruler, president, Müller-Bees Inschriften der jüdischen Katakombe am Monteverde No.14

ἐξαύξω.definition: increase, Thphr.CP1.22.1:—Pass., grow too fast, Id.HP6.6.6

ἐξαφαιρέω.definition: take away:—Med., Od.22.444, cf. S.El.1157; Trag.Adesp.296; f.l. in D.8.42

ἐξαφύω.definition: draw forth, . . Od.14.95: poet. aor., Opp.H.1.573: Ep. fut. 3pl., Hsch

ἔξεδρος.definition: away from home, opp; c. gen., out of, away from, E.IT80: metaph., insensate words, Id.Hipp.935

ἐξεθισμός.definition: change of habit, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.1.7

ἐξειλύω.definition: unfold:—Pass., of serpents gliding along the ground, Theoc.24.17

ἔξειμι.definition: come forth to apply the test, S.Ph.98; but, submit to the test, Id.Fr.105; . . E.Fr.334

ἐξελαιόω.definition: make into oil, Thphr.CP6.8.1:—Pass., become oily, ib.6.7.4

ἐξελαύνω.definition: fut. Hdt.4.148, 5.63, IG12.39.4: pf; drive out horses, etc., out of the ranks of the Trojans, Il.5.324, cf. 10.499; E.Ph.1190:—Med., drive out one's horses, Theoc.24.119 ; lead out an army, Hdt.1.76, 7.38; A.R.1.987; …

ἐξέλκω.definition: fut. Ar.Eq.365 : aor. 1 inf. Id.Pax315, 506:—Pass., Hdt.2.70:— draw, drag out, Il.23.762: c. gen. loci, Od.5.432 ; . . E.Hec.544; rescue from slavery, Pi.P.1.75; of a lame man, S.Ph.291: abs., without of one wounded, …

ἐξεμέω.definition: pf. Aristid.Or.50.5 (v.l; abs., vomit, be sick, Ar.Ra.11

ἐξεναρίζω.definition: strip or spoil a foe slain in fight; kill, slay, Od.11.273; Il.6.30, cf. Hes.Th.289, B.5.146, Lyc.50, etc.—In Hom. more freq. than the simple Verb

ἐξερεείνω.definition: c. acc. rei, inquire into, Od.10.14; c. acc. pers., inquire after, . . 23.86; inquire of, A.R.4.1250: abs., make inquiry, Il.9.672, etc.:—Med., 10.81

ἐξερείπω.definition: strike off, Pi.P.4.264; more freq. intr. in aor. 2 inf. to earth, Il.14.414; the mane streaming downwards from the yoke-cushion, 17.440; letting their necks fall on the ground, Hes.Sc.174; fall down, Id.Th.704.—Mostly…

ἐξερέω.definition: Att. contr. fut. of :—I will speak out, tell out, utter aloud, Hom. always abs. in sg., Il.8.286, 12.215, Od.9.365, al.; in tmesi, Il.1.204, 233, al.: c. acc. in Trag., S.OT800, cf. 219, etc.: c. dupl. acc., Id.El.984…

ἐξέρομαι.definition: Ion. fut. aor. 2; c. acc. rei, inquire into a thing, Od.13.127; so also . . will inquire concerning him, what he is now about, S.Ph.439

ἐξερύω.definition: Ion. aor.1 Ep. and also :—draw out of, . . Il.5.112; . . Od.22.386, cf. Hdt.1.141; Il.16.505; snatch out of, 23.870; but . . by the foot, 10.490; draw out, 13.194; tear out, Od.18.87; Hdt.2.38

ἐξέρχομαι.definition: fut. supplies the fut., also impf. aor. 2 the only tense used in Hom.:-go or come out of, c. gen.loci, Il.22.237,413,417; 10.140; etc., A.Ch.663, S.El.778, etc.; . . Hdt.8.75, 9.12, S.OC37, etc.; . . E.Ph.476; of an a…

ἐξερωέω.definition: swerve from the course, of shy horses, Il.23.468; Theoc.25.189

ἐξευπορέω.definition: supply abundantly; abs., find a way out, ib.861b.—The form in X.An.5.6.19, is prob. f.l. for

ἐξεύρεσις.definition: searching out, search, Hdt.1.67; finding out, invention, ib.94

ἐξευρίσκω.definition: fut. aor. 2 Med; seek out, search after, Id.7.119,5.33

ἐξέψω.definition: boil thoroughly, Hdt.4.61:—Pass., to be boiled out, v.l. in Arist.Mete.384a2

ἐξηγέομαι.definition: to be leader of, c. gen. pers; c. acc. pers., lead, govern, in Th., 1.76; ib.71

ἐξηθέω.definition: filter out, purify, in Pass., Arist.Pr.967a15, Thphr.CP6.13.1

ἐξήκω.definition: to have reached a certain point; of prophecies, dreams, etc., to have come to an accomplishment, turn out true, Hdt.1.120, 6.80; S.OT1182; of magical operations, succeed, PMag.Par.1.1273

ἐξηχέω.definition: sound forth, LXXJl.3.14, Nech. ap; utter senseless sounds, of idiots, Polem.Phgn.51

ἔξηχος.definition: rudely sounding: hence, absurd, stupid, Porph.Chr.35, EM696.39

ἐξίημι.definition: send out, let one go out; intr., of rivers, discharge themselves, Hdt.1.6 , al., Th.4.103

ἐξιθύνω.definition: make straight, Il.15.410; direct aright, A.R.1.562

ἐξικνέομαι.definition: poet. aor. Il.9.479, augm; come to as a suppliant, c. acc. pers., Od.13.206, 20.223, Pi.P.11.35; Ant.Lib.38.2

ἐξιόω.definition: clean from rust, Arr.Epict.4.11.13; make poisonous, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.104

ἐξιπόω.definition: press or squeeze out, Hp.Art.50; dry thoroughly, Aristid.Or.36.69:—Pass., prob.l. in Ps.-Democr.Alch.p.44 B

ἐξισόω.definition: make equal or even, bring to a level with; Pass., is levelled, equalized, i.e. resolved in harmony, S.El.1072 ; lit., levelled, J.BJ5.3.5

ἐξισχύω.definition: have strength enough, be able; c. gen., fate prevailing over the children, Ael.VH6.13, cf. Steph.in Hp.1.71D

ἐξίσχω.definition: intr., stand out, project, Paus.5.12.1; prominent eyes, Hp.Prog.2, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.27; of bones, Aret.SA2.8

ἔξογκος.definition: prominent, Plu.Fr.inc.149, cf. Steph.in Hp.1.187 D

ἐξοδεία.definition: prob. for expedition, Plb.4.54.3; procession from the shrines, OGI90.42

ἐξοδία.definition: Ion. marching out, expedition; journey, PSI4.406.27

ἐξόζω.definition: intr., smell, smell; c. gen., smell of a thing, Thphr.Od.20

ἐξοίχομαι.definition: to have gone out, to be quite gone, Il.6.379,384, S.OC867; Pl.Com.69.11: metaph., Antipho Soph.49; Pl.R.503c

ἐξόλλυμι.definition: and fut. aor. 1 pf; Med., with pf. 2 perish utterly, Emp.11.3, S.Tr.84, Ar.Pax366, Pl.l.c., etc.; . . Ar.Pax483: opt. in imprecations, Id.Fr.105; Alex.120

ἐξομματόω.definition: open the eyes of; metaph., make clear or plain, A.Pr.499

ἐξονομαίνω.definition: name, speak of by name, Il.3.166; . . name, tell it, Od.6.66, cf. h.Ven.252; SIG527.122

ἐξονυχίζω.definition: try a thing's smoothness by drawing the; deprive of the base of the petal, Orib.5.33.1; of lilies, in Pass., Aët.1.115

ἐξοπτάω.definition: bake thoroughly; metaph., of love, S.Fr.474.3

ἐξοράω.definition: see from afar:—Pass; have the appearance, Hp.Morb.2.68

ἐξοργιάζω.definition: excite to mystic frenzy; intr., become frenzied, ib.p.26 K

ἐξόριος.definition: out of the bounds of one's; Subst., , exile, Marcellin.Vit. Thuc.47, Eust.1161.35

ἐξόριστος.definition: expelled, banished; put beyond the borders, of the dead body of a criminal, . . Din.1.77

ἐξορμάω.definition: send forth, send to war, A.Pers.46, E.IT1437; intr., like Pass., set out, start, esp. in haste, Od.12.221; X.An.5.7.17: c. gen., set out from, E.Tr.1131, etc.: metaph., break out, S.Tr.1089

ἔξορμος.definition: sailing from a harbour, c. gen; issuing forth, dub. l. in Arist.PA694a23

ἐξοφέλλω.definition: increase exceedingly, offered higher and higher dowry, Od.15.18

ἐξυμενίζω.definition: strip off the skin or membrane, Dsc.2.76.1; Archig. ap. Aët.16.48

ἐξυπανίστημι.definition: only in intr. aor. 2, a weal started up from under the skin of the back, Il.2.267, cf. Pythag. ap. Porph.VP40

ἐξυπτιάζω.definition: turn a person quite on the back; intr., lie back, of the horns of wild cattle, Id.HA499a7

ἔξω.definition: with Verbs of motion, out or out of, Od.14.526; Hdt.1.10; Pl.Phdr.247b; D.18.323; Luc.Alex.38, etc

ἐξωθέω.definition: aor. 1 , thrust out, force; put forth painful words, break forth into cruel words, S.Ph.1142

ἐξωμίας.definition: one with arms bare to the shoulder, Luc.Vit.Auct.7

ἐξωριάζω.definition: leave out of thought, neglect, f.l. for A.Pr.17

ἔξωσις.definition: putting out, displacement, Hp.Art.46; thrust, Marcellin.Puls.99

ἐξώστρα.definition: stage-machine identified with the; bridge thrust out from the besiegers' tower against the walls of the besieged place, Lat. exostra, Veget.de Re Milit.4.21

ἐξώφορος.definition: brought out, published; tending outwards, Marcellin.Puls.65

ἐπαγάλλομαι.definition: Pass., glory in, exult in, c. dat., Il.16.91, cf. Q.S.7.327, Tryph.671; Crates Theb.4; Them.Or.11.151c; Artem.3.31; X.Oec.4.17

ἐπαγείρω.definition: gather together, collect, of things, Il.1.126:—Pass., of men, assemble, Od.11.632, cf. Pi.P.9.54

ἐπαγοράζω.definition: purchase a title to the next vacancy of a priesthood, SIG1014.17

ἐπάγω.definition: set on, urge on, as hunters do dogs, Od.19.445, cf. X.Cyn.10.19:— in Med., ib.6.25

ἐπαγωγή.definition: bringing on or to; bringing in to one's aid, introduction, Id.3.100, cf. 82 ; introduction of food through the gullet, Arist.Spir.483a9

ἐπαέξω.definition: make to grow, prosper, Od.14.65:— Pass., increase, grow, Semon.7.85 , Nic.Th.449

ἐπαιάζω.definition: cry over, mourn over; join in the wail, Bion1.2, etc.; Luc.Luct.20

ἐπαιγίζω.definition: rush upon, twice in Hom. of a stormy wind, . . Il.2.148; . . Od.15.293; Alciphr.3.42: metaph., AP5.285 : c. dat., rush over, of a stream that has burst its banks, Opp.C.2.125: c. acc., of the dolphin, Id.H.2.583

ἐπαινέω.definition: Aeol. Simon.5.19; Lacon; praise, commend in any way , or Alc.37A, Hdt.3.34,6.130; E.Hipp.264; commend one for a thing, but in this case the thing is always a neut. Pron. or Adj., A.Pr.342 ; S.Aj.1381, cf. Pl.Smp.222a;…

ἐπαίρω.definition: Ion. and poet. Hdt.1.204 and always in; lift, raise, 10.80; S.Ph.889; Id.OT1276 codd.; E.Tr.99 ; Ar.V.996; Amphis l.c.; SIG1109.24; IG3.1132; D.18.291; opp. Plu.Luc.3:—Med., didst lift and put me to thy breast, A.R.3.…

ἐπαιτέω.definition: beg as a mendicant, Id.OC1364, cf. E.Rh.715: abs., Vett.Val.68.30, Luc.Asin.35

ἐπακούω.definition: fut. ib.Ge.30.33, later Psalm.Solom.18.3:-hear, c. acc. rei, of the Sun, Il.3.277, cf. Od.11.109; prov., as thou speakest, so wilt thou be answered, Il.20.250; Hes.Op.448; Ar.Eq.1080: c. acc. rei et gen. pers., Od.19.…

ἐπακρίζω.definition: reach the top of a thing, he reached the farthest point in deeds of blood, of Orestes, A.Ch.932

ἐπαλάομαι.definition: wander about or over, Od.4.81; ib.83: subj. aor. 15.401

ἐπαλαστέω.definition: to be full of wrath at a thing, Od.1.252, cf. A.R.3.369,557

ἐπάλειψις.definition: painting over of colours; smearing over, anointing, EM69.41

ἐπαλέξω.definition: Ep. Verb, defend, succour, Il.8.365; ward off, keep off, Il.20.315

ἐπαληθεύω.definition: prove true, substantiate, verify; prove one's right to, Ph.2.6, 263

ἐπαλλάσσω.definition: Att. change over: once in Hom; intr., alternate, interlocking teeth, Arist.PA661b18; of leaves, dub. in Thphr.HP4.6.10

ἐπαμαξεύω.definition: = traverse with cars, . . marked with the tracks of wheels, S.Ant.251

ἐπαμβατήρ.definition: poet. for one who mounts upon, assailant: metaph., of leprous eruptions, A.Ch.280

ἐπαμείβω.definition: exchange, barter, Il.6.230; Orph.A.422:—Med., come one after another, come in turn to, Il.6.339; Archil.9.9

ἐπαμύνω.definition: come to aid, succour, Il.6.361; ward off, v.l. for in AP5.6

ἐπανάγω.definition: bring up: hence; stir up, excite, Hdt.7.160

ἐπανατίθημι.definition: lay upon, Ar.V.148; Med., shift one's position, of patients under operation, Gal.18.425

ἐπανατολή.definition: invisible rising of stars just after sunrise or sunset, Ptol.Alm.8.4

ἐπαναφορά.definition: referring, reference; reference of a question to an assembly, And.3.33; to the people, Harp

ἐπάνθημα.definition: efflorescence, fine flower, Id.in Nic.p.39 P., al.; special virtues, ib.p.118 P

ἐπανίστημι.definition: set up again, ib.778d; make to rise against, Plu.Sert.13; raise in revolt against, App.Hisp.101

ἐπανύω.definition: fut. complete, accomplish, Hes.Sc.311:—Med., procure, . . codd. in S.Tr.995 ; carry into effect, Ph.1.77

ἐπαξιόω.definition: think right, deem it right, c. inf; expect, believe, c. acc. et inf., . . . . ib.658; but . . deems thee worthy of honour, so as to render thee a due return, Id.OC1497

ἐπαπειλέω.definition: hold out as a threat to one; c. dat. only, threaten, Il.13.582

ἐπαπορέω.definition: raise a new doubt or question; c. dat., criticize, Diog.Oen.18

ἐπαραρίσκω.definition: aor. 1 aor. 2 to or; intr. in Ion. pf. plpf. tight or exactly, a cross-bolt was fitted therein, Il.12.456; part. close-fitting, well fixed, firm on his feet, Arat.83: also Ep. aor. part. Pass., well-fitted, prepared, …

ἐπαρήγω.definition: come to aid, help, Il.23.783, Od.13.391, E.El.1350 , Ar.V.402: abs., A.Ch.725 ; S.El.1197; also in Prose, X.Cyr.6.4.18, LXX2 Ma.13.17

ἐπαρκέω.definition: fut. : Ep. aor. inf; c. acc. rei, ward off, prevent, A.R.2.1161; S.Aj.360

ἐπαρτάω.definition: hang on or over; the elevated part of the beam, Arist.Mech.850a23

ἐπαρτύω.definition: and fit or fix on; prepare, Od.3.152; Opp.C.2.443:—Med., they prepared them a meal, h.Cer.128

ἐπαρυστήρ.definition: vessel for pouring oil into a lamp, LXXEx.25.37

ἐπαρύτω.definition: draw a liquid from one vessel into another, metaph. in Med., Plu.2.600d:—Act., dub. in D.Chr.12.70

ἐπαρχία.definition: the government of an or the; military 'command', force occupying a district, Ph.Bel.96.49

ἐπάρχω.definition: rule over, X.Cyr.4.6.2; rule besides one's hereditary dominions, X.Cyr.1.1.4

ἐπασκέω.definition: labour or toil at, prepare or finish; adorn, exalt, Pi.N.9.10, cf. Fr.194.4; Id.Parth.2.71

ἐπαύλημα.definition: musical phrase played on the flute, EM757.32

ἐπαυρέω.definition: Act., partake of, share, c.gen. rei, . . Il.18.302; . . Od.17.81; enjoys a greater share of night, of Sirius, Hes.Op.419; many have had enjoyment of neighbours, Pi.P.3.36; have enjoyment in the highest degree, Thgn.11…

ἐπαύω.definition: shout over, A.Ch.828 codd. ; in Theoc.23.44 is dub

ἐπαχλύω.definition: trans., darken, Them.Or.11.144c:—Pass., ib.19.232d. even in pres., A.R. l.c.; in Arat.906 Schneider restored for

ἐπεγείρω.definition: awaken, rouse up, Od.22.431, Thgn.469; erect, raise, erecting his prickles, like certain fish when irritated, Com.Adesp.1338 ; Philum.Ven.17.5

ἐπεγκλίνω.definition: incline, turn towards either side, v.l. in Gal.UP12.9

ἐπεγχύτης.definition: cup-bearer, so called by the Hellespontines, Demetr.Sceps. ap. Ath.10.425c

ἐπείγω.definition: Il.12.452, etc., Aeol. Hdn.Gr.2.436; drive on, urge forward, . . Od.12.205; freq. of a fair wind, 12.167; Il.15.382; S.Ph.1451

ἐπίδρομος.definition: that may be overrun, a wall; metaph., intelligible, Them.Or.13.162c

ἐπιτήκω.definition: melt upon, pour when melted over a thing, Hdt.7.239; Plu.Ages.40

ἐπιτίθημι.definition: Pass. mostly furnished by; set upon, turn towards, Il.10.46; but c. inf., put it into her mind to.., Od.21.1

ἐπιτίμιον.definition: mostly in pl., value; the honours paid to a person, S.El.915

ἐπιφώσκω.definition: = grow towards daylight, dawn; trans., let shine forth, Poet.de herb.24

ἐπιχορεύω.definition: dance to or in honour of a thing; add a chorus or choral song, Philostr.VA5.14

ἐπιχράω.definition: touch on the surface, graze, c. gen., .. A.R.2.283: c. acc., Q.S.11.480

ἐπιχρίω.definition: anoint, besmear, (sc; plaster over, with a thing, Luc.Hist.Conscr.62

ἐπίχρυσος.definition: overlaid or plated with gold; rich, prob. for Hld.2.8

ἐπιψαίρω.definition: skim the surface of a thing, Opp.H.4.512

ἐπογμεύω.definition: trace a furrow: hence, metaph of dancing, Tryph.354

ἐποπτεύω.definition: overlook, watch, of an overseer; visit, punish, A.Eu.220

ἐπόπτης.definition: overseer, watcher, esp. of; simply, spectator, A.Pr.301
